entries.lead: Publishing as maintainer-run and hosted submission need an explicit opt-in
entries.text: benchbox publish run and benchbox run --publish now refuse the maintainer-run trust label, which is also their default, unless BENCHBOX_ALLOW_MAINTAINER_LABEL=1 is set, and a non-interactive benchbox submit --service is refused unless --acknowledge-hosted-submission or BENCHBOX_ACKNOWLEDGE_HOSTED_SUBMISSION=1 is set.
details: Both refusals exit 6 before anything is uploaded or copied. Publishing under another label, such as community-submission, and submitting with --dry-run need no opt-in.
Scripts and CI jobs that publish as maintainer-run or upload with --service must set the variable or pass the flag. An interactive terminal session is not asked to acknowledge a hosted submission.

entries.text: ~/.benchbox is now created with mode 0700 and credentials.yaml is written through a private temporary file with mode 0600, so the saved credentials are never readable by other local users, even briefly.
details: A wider existing credentials file is tightened on the next save, with a one-line warning, and a failure to create the file privately is now an error instead of being ignored.
The file is still plain text. ${VAR} references in it are now kept as written when BenchBox saves the file again instead of being replaced by the secret's value.

entries.text: Prompts that need an answer now exit cleanly with a message when there is no terminal: benchbox setup --remove (new --yes), export overwrite (--force), publish remove (--yes) exit 6, and benchbox run --non-interactive no longer offers credential setup after a credential failure.
details: benchbox auth login and refresh without a token keep exiting 1 with the existing message when nothing can be read.
benchbox publish help now shows benchbox publish run in its examples and tip.
